correctness.rationale: For every fixed peer configuration and public risk r, only the event of exactly m−1 peer cooperators makes focal contribution change the disaster outcome. Conditional expected difference is bp(r)r−c. One incumbent risk cutoff makes p(r) piecewise constant, so there is at most one strict-positive interval per piece. Exactly two separated windows iff c/(bp−)<τ<c/(bp+)<1 with p−,p+>0. The unrestricted optimum is pointwise; differentiation of every upper-tail expected gain shows only two candidate maxima, yielding exact gap min{bp−(τ−α)^2/2,bp+(γ−τ)^2/2}. The 21-person witness enumerates all 190 equally likely unordered peer pairs and integrates rational affine segments: p−=10/19, p+=18/95, α=3/10, γ=5/6, E−=E+=b/95, H=b/380 and optimal gap b/95. Analytical proof handles all real risk thresholds; the optional numerical grid cannot substitute for it.

value.rationale: The restricted monotone tolerance is central to a fresh shared-risk game model. A sharp condition shows when the restriction creates a genuine private inefficiency and the mechanism (a drop in pivotality when other adaptive peers simultaneously cooperate) is structurally distinct from ordinary higher-risk/higher-cooperation reasoning. The exact 21-person witness gives two nontrivial risk windows and fivefold difference between optimal and best monotone gains relative to never contributing. This is a motivated classification rather than a generic numerical slice; no downstream theorem or evolutionary dynamics are claimed.
